reviewer: root, independent of the proof author
scope: Second finite-level Selmer estimate for the original W2, preserving its local conditions and quantifiers.

audit_groups.finding: The paired algebra has epsilon_i epsilon_prime_j=delta_ij eta. Its adjoint action on exactly W2=epsilon_prime E+eta O gives the mixed commutator defect. The cyclotomic polarization scalar is retained and cancels in the adjoint action.
Polarized input cocycles extend uniquely with value zero at c, without altering their prescribed restrictions. No normalization by an arbitrary input coboundary is used.

The actual w1 basis change gives Z+sum[Y_j,P_j]. Odd coordinates have zero diagonal even for interleaved types. Thus the input even mu-diagonal condition is preserved. At old places a continuous unramified lift exists and all corrections vanish on inertia.

A vanishing original obstruction class gives a genuine W2 cocycle with the required local primitives. Adding d(Psi0(c)/2), with a plus sign, kills its value at c; shifting each local primitive by the same vector preserves the local conditions.

The all-quotient bound and finite obstruction generator lemma yield a unit-containing combination multiplied by t^C2. The constant is fixed before m; the sufficiently large tower level depends on m and works for all input tuples.
This supplies the second finite-level estimate under the original arithmetic system and normalized point. It does not construct those objects or the patched automorphic modules.

negative_controls: Dropping the mixed epsilon-epsilon' product changes the actual action.
The even ordinary diagonal restriction cannot be supplied by an odd eta correction.
Characteristic2 can obstruct the cyclic lift; oddness and the division by2 are retained.
The wrong complex-conjugation normalization sign is rejected by the finite cocycle suite.

limits: Arithmetic realization, normalized points and patched automorphic modules remain required.
Finite exact checks supplement the general human proof. No Lean build and no whole-node closure.
